items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-11-17
items.q: I played taps at his funeral.

ctx.x: Tell him I heard he had a fight with Corny.

Say, he heard you had a fight with Corny. I think I heard about that. I think it was on my birthday that night, I got drunk, you know. And Tony told me to stop playing, you know. Stop drinking. I said, oh, you ain't got nothing to do with me. I said, the white people, they was giving it to me, helping me to celebrate. And Tony got mad. I said, you big son got busted. I said, go ahead, sit on, sit on, sit on. And then after he told me to come over, you know. Zip would play with his dad, you know. You know Zip,…
Tell him I heard that when Cornish swung at him, he'd run between his legs.

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1960-01-21
items.q: And then Guy Kelly, he went up there with Guy, he said Guy Kelly, drink, you know. He said, drink, yeah. And he said, I don't like me and stuff. Bad, you know, bootlegger. That must have hit Guy Kelly's stomach up.

ctx.x: I asked him which came first.

We had some band, too. Most of our jobs called for white people. We said. We was up three years before we could play for one color people. And the first time we played for color people when Joe Oliver left from the air. You know, the thing I got in there when I was standing right by Joe Oliver with a fellow drumming him, Buddy Sali. Hit him in the eye with a wheel by the hammer. And you know, I thought Joe would be one eye, you know. And he used to have a man, Carol, all them boys. He must have been around about…
I asked you who this Bourne was. That's not Harrison Bourne.

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-12-11
items.q: I was with Guy when he died. ... I played caps at his funeral. ... But Guy, well, we used to go to rehearsals

ctx.x: Most people say Buddy when you put them on the spot.

Louis couldn't believe it. Louis used to recognize Guy Kelly, didn't it? Louis, didn't he recognize Guy Kelly? Uh, not much. No. Everybody say Guy Kelly was next to him. No. I was with Guy when he died. When he left here, he was good. But when he got up there, he got so he couldn't play nothing much. Uh, you know what I meant to lick it? I know. I want to see what I'm talking about. You used to sit like that? I played caps at his funeral. He did die just that time about four times, not behind one another. And…
Ask him who Crowback worked with. Crowback? Yeah, Crowback.
